title: Bundle compliance and surgical site infection after colorectal resection: a prospective observational study with post-discharge surveillance
abstract: Objective: to measure element-level and full bundle compliance and estimate the association of full compliance with 30-day surgical site infection. Design: prospective observational study of all colorectal resections over 24 months. Results will be written after data collection.
introduction: Bundles are associated with fewer infections after colorectal surgery in mostly uncontrolled studies. Local delivery of each element and its association with infection, including infections after discharge, are unknown.
methods: Theatre staff recorded each element on a two-minute form, and full compliance was scored all-or-none over applicable elements. Surveillance nurses followed every patient for 30 days with a day-30 call, and logistic regression adjusted for six pre-specified covariates.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present element-level and full compliance for elective and emergency cases, infection rates and the adjusted association.
discussion: The discussion will interpret the association as an association and note that the cited multicentre record failed an identity check and must be re-appraised. It will consider recording effects and confounding by emergency status.
limitations: The design is observational and confounded by emergency status. Recording may itself change practice.
conclusion: To be written after analysis. It will describe compliance and an adjusted association, not the effect of individual elements.
